title: Selective prefetch & burst attenuation playbook
creator: Lena Chow
description: Playbook to implement a coordinated burst attenuation mechanism that combines short-window probabilistic admission (p-drop), tenant credit windows, and selective prefetch suppression to protect SLOs during multi-region spikes and partial outages. This ticket covers design decisions, implementation tasks, test and canary rollout, monitoring, and operator runbook for graceful degradation modes that minimize global availability loss while preserving best-effort latency for high-priority tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic admission controller that supports per-tenant credit windows, short-term probabilistic drops, and a configurable partial-response folding policy implemented in the runtime
Integration tests and chaos tests that show <5% SLO violations (p99 latency and error budget) under 3x baseline burst for top-50 tenants in simulated multi-region failover
Operator runbook with clear alerts and automated fallback (regional circuit-breaker -> distilled-model fallback -> prefetch suppression) documented in Confluence
Canary rollout plan validated on one dedicated pool and one hosted region with automated metrics gating and rollback on defined thresholds
tasks: Design: finalize admission controller API, credit-window semantics, and probabilistic drop strategy (owner: Miguel)
Runtime: implement short-window p-drop hook and token-aware partial-response folding (owner: Core Runtime Team)
Console: add per-tenant credit view and override panel in Redwood Console (owner: Console Team)
E2E tests: create multi-region load generator and scripted failover scenarios (owner: SRE)
Metrics: emit tenant_credit_utilization, p_drop_rate, attenuation_mode, partial_response_rate, distilled_fallback_count
Docs: write operator runbook and customer-facing degradation guidance (owner: Product Docs)
PR: land implementation behind a feature flag; include feature-flag gating in configs
decisions: Use sliding credit windows (default 60s) with burn and refill rates per tenant instead of fixed token buckets to better capture burstiness across multiplexed clients
Probabilistic drop (p-drop) will be applied at admission with a tunable sigmoid curve based on short-window occupancy and recent p99 latency to avoid step functions
Partial-response folding (return intermediate answers or embeddings-only) is opt-in per-model and will be driven by client hint headers to preserve client UX where supported
Cross-region circuit-breaker will trigger attenuation mode by signaling runtime with a tiered escalation: soft-attenuation -> aggressive p-drop -> distilled-model fallback -> region quarantine
Prefetch will be suppressed for requests from tenants in aggressive attenuation mode to reduce KV cache churn and token spend
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff completed, prototype design sketch reviewed with Runtime and SRE; agreed on metrics list and initial thresholds
2025-02-27: Runtime team merged p-drop hook and feature flag scaffolding; initial unit tests green; feature gated behind ff_admission_attenuation
2025-03-03: SRE simulated 2x burst with p-drop at 10% baseline; observed 18% reduction in tail latency for non-attenuated tenants; working on broader test matrix
2025-03-05: Console mockups complete; credit override UX needs legal review for enterprise exemptions
test_plan: Create deterministic load scenarios targeted at top-50 tenants and synthetic low-priority tenants. Run 3 classes of tests: baseline (1x), burst (3x), and failover (simulate region latency spike + 50% capacity loss). For each run verify metrics: p99 latency, error rate, token burn per tenant, and percent requests served as partial responses. Include chaos test where circuit-breaker toggles and ensure automated rollback triggers if customer-visible error increase >0.5%.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind ff_admission_attenuation. 2) Enable in a single dedicated pool for non-production workloads. 3) Canary in one hosted region for 2% of traffic (low-priority tenants only). 4) Gradual ramp to 20% then 50% with metric gates: no increase in high-priority tenant p99>300ms and global error rate delta <0.2%. 5) Global rollout with staggered regional enabling and final console default set to 'opt-out' for enterprise exempt tenants.
monitoring: Dashboard: Attenuation Overview with per-region, per-tenant credit utilization and p-drop heatmap
Alert: High p_drop_rate (>40% sustained for 60s) -> P0 alert to SRE
Alert: Top-10 tenant token-burn increased >2x compared to 24h baseline -> P1 alert to Product Ops
SLO Gate: If high-priority tenant p99 latency increases >10% vs baseline for 5m during canary, auto-roll back feature flag
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive p-drop could increase client retries and overall work; Mitigation: Sigmoid tuning, client-backoff advisory, and circuit-breaker to flip to distilled fallback instead of 100% drop
Risk: Prefetch suppression may harm cold-start latency for some latency-sensitive tenants; Mitigation: Allow whitelist/enterprise overrides and staged rollout with telemetry
Risk: Cross-region signaling latency could cause inconsistent attenuation decisions; Mitigation: use local short-window heuristics and bounded staleness (~5s) for escalation decisions
Risk: UX confusion when clients receive partial responses; Mitigation: versioned partial-response schema and clear developer docs + example SDK handling
operator_runbook: Operator steps: 1) Identify attenuation events from dashboard. 2) Check tenant_credit_utilization and p_drop_rate. 3) If soft-attenuation active, monitor p99 and error rate for top-10 tenants. 4) If thresholds breached, either increase credit refill for affected tenant or escalate to distilled fallback. 5) To manual rollback: toggle ff_admission_attenuation -> feature-flag off, observe metrics for 10 minutes, then re-evaluate. 6) If region quarantine required, follow multi-region failover doc and trigger regional circuit-breaker.
notes_for_reviews: Focus review on credit window semantics (60s default) and partial-response contract. Confirm Console UX for overrides includes audit logging. Security team to review distilled-model fallback for potential data-leakage modes (currently flagged for a separate short review).
final_comment: This playbook aims to add a middle-ground attenuation that preserves high-priority tenant SLOs while reducing noisy neighbor impact during spikes. Implementation should prioritize observability and reversibility.
